note: Nine books on the same shelf, in publication order. Titles, authors and years only — no sales figures, no rankings, nothing that would need a source beyond the books themselves. `line` is a one-sentence gloss and is our characterisation, not a quotation.
source: Publication details as printed on each first edition.

shelf.title: Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds
shelf.author: Charles Mackay
shelf.line: Tulips, the South Sea, the railway boom. People go mad in herds and recover one at a time.

shelf.title: A Random Walk Down Wall Street
shelf.author: Burton Malkiel
shelf.line: A blindfolded monkey throwing darts would do about as well as the experts.

shelf.title: Manias, Panics and Crashes
shelf.author: Charles Kindleberger
shelf.line: Every bubble runs the same script. Knowing the script does not tell you the date.

shelf.title: Irrational Exuberance
shelf.author: Robert Shiller
shelf.line: Published the same month the dot-com market peaked. The one that landed.

shelf.title: Fooled by Randomness
shelf.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
shelf.line: You cannot tell skill from luck by looking at the winners.

shelf.title: The Black Swan
shelf.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
shelf.line: The events that matter most are the ones nobody had on the list.

shelf.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
shelf.author: Daniel Kahneman
shelf.line: The mind is built to see a story where there is only noise.

shelf.title: The Signal and the Noise
shelf.author: Nate Silver
shelf.line: The book that made forecasting famous. Its actual argument is mostly humility.

shelf.title: Superforecasting
shelf.author: Tetlock & Gardner
shelf.line: Some people really are better at this. They give odds, and they change them.
